Subject: Dedicated capacity: initial ops handover & burst strategy

Hi Chandra / Priya —

Thanks again for the productive kickoff last week. Per our onboarding plan, this thread will capture the operational handoff items for Primis AI's Dedicated GPU pool. I've attached a short model inventory and our proposed SLO matrix so we can align on capacity and fallback behaviors.

Key asks from Redwood to Primis before our activation sprint:
- Confirm peak concurrent requests per minute (90th percentile) for the first 30 days.
- Call out any latency SLOs per model (p50 / p95) and which models may tolerate quantization/8-bit variants.
- Any regulatory constraints for data locality (required region(s)).

Our initial recommendations (high-level):
- Start with a 12-GPU pool (A100/80GB equiv) with a 25% baseline headroom for steady-state.
- Autoscale triggers: add nodes at 70% sustained GPU utilization, scale in at <35% for 10m.
- Burst policy: allow cross-region burst to us-west-2 only for stateless workloads; stateful KV-cache workloads must remain in primary region.
- Prewarm: spin 2 thin instances per model during business hours for 50ms cold-start target.

Attachments: primis_model_inventory.csv, primis_slo_matrix.xlsx

Next steps: if you can confirm the three asks above by EOD Fri (11/27), Monica will draft the activation sprintcard and Jonas will schedule the ops handoff call.

Best,

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial ops handover & burst strategy

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. We reviewed the attachments and have preliminary answers below.

- Peak concurrent requests: currently 420 RPM for the inference endpoint (90th perc, observed in our staged load tests). We expect a 30–40% increase after marketing ramp in month 1.
- Latency SLOs: p50 target 60ms, p95 target 220ms. The recommendation to use 8-bit for reranker models is acceptable; the production ranking model must stay FP16 for quality reasons.
- Data locality: must remain within US (no cross-border replication). Cross-region burst (us-west-2) is OK for stateless feature-extraction models.

Two clarifying questions:
1) For autoscale we need the minimum time-to-add-node assumption — does Redwood assume 3–5 minutes to add a preprovisioned instance, or longer?
2) Can the burst policy be restricted to only run on a different model variant (smaller) during cross-region bursts to guarantee quality control?

We'll confirm the final numbers after an internal sync tomorrow and will upload a finalized model list.

Thanks,
Chandra
Head of Platform Engineering
Primis AI
chandra@primis.ai

Chandra — appreciate the quick answers. To address your questions and lock a runnable plan, here's the ops-runbook-level proposal we'll use for the activation sprint. This will be included in the sprintcard and turned into the final SOW/DocuSign link after you sign off.

1) Node provisioning time
- Warm pool instances: we will preprovision a set of warm nodes that can be attached to the pool in ~90–180s. Cold node provisioning (full image + cache) is longer (~6–8 min).
- Recommendation: maintain a warm buffer of 2 GPUs per region for the first 14 days. That meets the 3–5 minute practical window for scaling effective capacity because attachment + container start is fast once warmed.

2) Autoscale policy (detailed)
- Scale-up: trigger when average GPU utilization > 70% over a 120s window OR request queue latency > 300ms for 60s. Add nodes in increments of 2 GPUs.
- Scale-down: evaluate every 10m; scale in if utilization < 35% and queue latency < 150ms. Drain connections for 90s before shutdown.

3) Burst and variant strategy
- Cross-region burst allowed for stateless models only; for stateful/latency-sensitive models, no burst.
- Variant mapping: during cross-region burst, we automatically route to a quantized (8-bit) or small-variant model if customer opts in. We'll provide a model-variant mapping file for approval.

4) Prewarm & KV-caching
- Prewarm 2 instances per high-throughput model during peak hours (09:00–18:00 PT) and keep a shared KV-cache pool with a 5-minute TTL for reuse across sessions.

5) Operational guardrails
- Maintenance windows: Sundays 02:00–05:00 PT (non-overlapping with Primis batch jobs).
- Fallback: secondary region = us-west-2, only after automated health checks and with explicit rate-limits to 30% of normal capacity.

Attachments: sow_v1.docx (draft SOW, includes acceptance criteria and SLA language)

If this looks good, please confirm by EOD Fri (11/27). We will then:
- Jonas will create the rollout timeline and backout plan.
- I will add the autoscale rules to the sprintcard and request engineering capacity for the warm buffer.

Regards,

Chandra / Priya — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clarifications. Two quick operational confirmations before we finalize the DocuSign:

1) Warm buffer: Primis confirmed they accept 2 warm GPUs in us-east-1 and a secondary warm buffer (1 GPU) in us-west-2 for burst — we will size the initial pool to 13 GPUs to accommodate the warm buffer and the baseline.
2) Variant routing: Primis opted in to the quantized variant for feature-extractors only; ranking model remains FP16 in-region.

I've created the activation timeline in the shared Drive folder and kick-off calendar invite for the handoff call next Tuesday, 11/30 at 10:00 AM PT (30m). Please review the SOW in Drive and sign via DocuSign when ready: https://app.docusign.com/schedules/DEAL-4892
